We propose giving one named external color specialist access to full-resolution master images from the first batch only. Seeing the whole sheet helps the specialist check whether color is consistent from edge to edge. We’ll submit the specialist’s name for your written approval and bind them to the studio’s confidentiality and deletion terms before granting access. They would work in a view-only workspace with downloads disabled. We’ll log access and revoke it as soon as calibration is complete, within three days of granting it. If full-sheet access is too broad, would you approve selected margin crops and color-target images?

Within the studio, only the assigned scanning and quality-control staff would have access. We propose keeping working files for ten calendar days after delivery of each batch so we can correct scans. We’ll delete the working files at the end of day ten. Encrypted backup copies would then expire through rotation within a further 45 days, so the last copy would expire by day 55 after delivery. Only designated administrators could access backups for disaster recovery. If a recovery restores a deleted file, we’ll delete it again before staff regain access. We can confirm both the working-file deletion and final backup expiry in writing.

For publicity, we’d like permission to publish one anonymized image showing the scanning process. We propose framing the equipment and color target so no donor handwriting, identifying details, or readable letter text appears. We’ll submit the exact image, caption, and intended publication channel for your written approval before use. Would that review process work for the archive?

**External specialist access: we cannot agree to full-resolution masters, and the limit depends on the collection.**

- **Two restricted collections:** the donor terms prohibit any third-party viewing of handwriting or identifying content. No external specialist or subcontractor may see any image of these letters, including margin crops. Only your assigned scanning and quality-control staff may handle them, and the schedule should say so in place of the general subcontractor clause.
- **All other collections:** one named specialist, approved by us in writing, may view masked images with handwriting and identifying content obscured. Your controls otherwise stand: view-only workspace, downloads disabled, logged access, revocation within three days.
- **Edge-to-edge color check:** we will supply a calibration sheet to be scanned across the full platen under the same settings. Color-target images are fine to share with the specialist. Does that, plus the masked images, give the specialist what they need? If not, tell us what specific measurement is missing.

**Retention: ten days for working files is acceptable, but 55 days for backups is too long.**

- **Working files:** these are deleted by the end of day ten after delivery of each batch. This replaces the open-ended "retained for quality control" wording.
- **Restricted collections:** can you exclude these from backup rotation entirely? We hold the originals and can re-supply for rescanning, so the disaster-recovery value is low.
- **Other collections:** we want the last backup copy to expire within 30 days of delivery. If your rotation cannot be shortened, say what the minimum is.
- **Restores:** your re-deletion commitment stands, and we would add notice to us of any restore that touches our files.

**Evidence of deletion and incident contact: both need to be in the signed schedule.**

- **Deletion certificate:** we need a written certificate for each batch, within two business days of working-file deletion and again at final backup expiry. It should give batch identifiers, file counts, date and method.
- **Access log:** we would receive the specialist access log when access is revoked.
- **Incident contact:** each side names a contact. You notify us within 24 hours of any suspected unauthorized access, loss, or disclosure, including by the specialist.

**Publicity: your review process works, with three conditions.**

- **Content:** the image shows equipment and the calibration sheet or color target only, with no donor material on the platen or in frame.
- **Caption:** it names no donor or collection.
- **Approval:** our written approval covers that one image, caption and channel, and any reuse needs fresh approval.

**Outstanding:**

1. Whether the restricted collections can be excluded from backups.
2. The backup expiry period for the other collections.
3. Whether the calibration sheet plus masked images is enough for the specialist.

Please also confirm whether any subcontractor other than the color specialist would touch any part of the pilot.

The full-platen calibration sheet scanned under the same settings, together with the permitted masked images, gives the specialist what they need for the first batch. No additional measurement is needed. The color specialist is the only subcontractor who would work on the pilot.

**Access.** We agree to replace the general subcontractor clause with the collection-specific terms. Only assigned studio scanning and quality-control staff may handle the two restricted collections or view any image of their letters, including crops. For other collections, our staff will mask handwriting and identifying content before placing an image in the specialist’s workspace. The specialist must be named, approved by the archive in writing, and bound by the confidentiality terms before access begins. Access will be view-only, with downloads disabled and access logged. We’ll revoke access when calibration ends, within three days of granting it, and send you the log at revocation.

**Retention.** We can exclude both restricted collections from backups entirely. Working files for every batch will be deleted by the end of calendar day ten after delivery. For other collections, our backup rotation requires 45 days from the last backup. We propose stopping new backups of each batch at delivery and keeping the ten-day correction workspace outside rotation. That makes **day 45 after delivery** the latest expiry. Corrections made after delivery would have no backup. If expiry by day 30 is essential, we can exclude those collections from backups too and rely on the archive to re-supply originals if rescanning is needed. Which arrangement should we put in the schedule for those collections?

**Evidence and incidents.** We’ll provide a certificate for each batch within two business days of working-file deletion and a second certificate at final backup expiry wherever backups exist. Each will specify batch identifiers, file counts, date, and method. For batches excluded from backup, the working-file certificate will confirm that no backup was created. We’ll notify you of any restore that touches archive files and re-delete any files due for deletion before staff regain access. Each side will name an incident contact in the signed schedule. We’ll notify yours within 24 hours of first becoming aware of suspected unauthorized access, loss, or disclosure, including an incident involving the specialist.

**Publicity.** We agree to all three conditions. The image will show only equipment and the calibration sheet or color target, with the platen and frame clear of donor material. The caption will name no donor or collection. We’ll obtain written approval for the exact image, caption, and channel before publication and fresh written approval for any reuse.

**Backups: exclude the other collections too.** No backups will be created for any pilot batch, and we will re-supply originals if rescanning is needed after a loss. That makes end of day ten after delivery the final deletion point for every batch, with one certificate per batch confirming deletion and that no backup was created.

One consequence for your restore clause: with no backups, it should not arise. Keep it as a safeguard, so if any archive file is found in a backup or restored, you notify our incident contact within 24 hours and delete it before staff regain access.

**The signed schedule should then contain:**

1. **Restricted collections:** only assigned studio scanning and quality-control staff may handle them or view any image, including crops. There is no subcontractor or specialist access. We will supply the two collection identifiers for the schedule.
2. **Other collections:** one named specialist, approved by us in writing and bound to the confidentiality terms before access, may see images masked by studio staff. Access is view-only with downloads disabled and logging, it is revoked within three days of grant, and the log comes to us at revocation.
3. **Calibration:** we supply the calibration sheet, which is scanned full-platen under the same settings. Color-target images may be shared with the specialist.
4. **Subcontractors:** there are none other than the named specialist. Any addition needs our prior written approval.
5. **Retention:** working files are deleted by the end of calendar day ten after delivery of each batch, and no backups are made. This replaces the "retained for quality control" wording.
6. **Evidence:** a deletion certificate for each batch within two business days, giving batch identifiers, file counts, date, method and confirmation that no backup was created.
7. **Incidents:** each side names a contact. You notify ours within 24 hours of becoming aware of suspected unauthorized access, loss or disclosure, including by the specialist.
8. **Publicity:** one image showing only equipment and the calibration sheet or color target, with no donor material in frame and no donor or collection named in the caption. Our written approval covers the exact image, caption and channel, and any reuse needs fresh approval.

**Outstanding before or after signature:**

- **Specialist:** no access begins until you submit the name and we approve it in writing.
- **Incident contacts:** both names and contact details must be inserted before signature.
- **Publicity image:** nothing is approved yet, and publication stays prohibited until we approve a specific submission.
- **Restricted collection identifiers:** we will send these for insertion.

Please confirm the no-backup arrangement and the eight items, and send the specialist's name and your incident contact.

We confirm the no-backup arrangement and agree to all eight items. We’ll exclude every pilot batch from backups, and the archive will re-supply originals if rescanning is needed after a loss. We’ll delete all working files by the end of calendar day ten after delivery of each batch and issue one certificate within two business days of deletion. It will record the batch identifiers, file counts, deletion date and method, and confirm that no backup was created.

We agree to the restore safeguard. If we discover an archive file in a backup or find that one has been restored, we’ll notify your incident contact within 24 hours of discovery and delete the file before staff regain access.

The specialist’s name and our incident contact’s name and contact details are pending. We’ll provide our incident contact details before signature. We’ll submit the specialist’s name for your written approval before granting any access. The specialist’s role is limited to first-batch calibration under the agreed controls. We’ll insert the two restricted collection identifiers when you supply them. Publication remains subject to your written approval of the exact image, caption, and channel.
